ranked.headline: Tissue-specific QTLs, splicing and functional assays pin GWAS variants to effector genes
ranked.summary: New preprints extend GWAS fine-mapping beyond expression to splicing, structural variants, allele-specific chromatin and MPRA/CRISPR validation in relevant cells.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is mapping disease-associated noncoding variants to effector genes in disease-relevant tissues and cell types. Several studies move beyond gene abundance. In 1,149 IBD colon samples, joint eQTL and sQTL mapping implicates NMD and immune pathways. Colocalization of 338 type 2 diabetes signals with adipose expression, splicing and transcript usage finds RNA features that gene-level eQTLs miss. Pangenome genotyping in CARTaGENE adds 103 structural-variant eQTLs. Functional resolution is reaching single variants. MPRA and CRISPR perturbation in chondrocytes link osteoarthritis variant rs1895062 to PAPPA. In human microglia, allele-specific open chromatin indicates that the alcohol use disorder variant rs7307261 alters ETS-factor binding. CELL-X prioritizes beta cells and genes such as SLC30A8 and TCF7L2 from islet single-cell data. The IGVF Catalog provides infrastructure by integrating 657 datasets. Studies of desert selection, hominin-derived variation and adipose transposable elements are more peripheral.

ranked.headline: Perturbation and spatial omics models increasingly account for measurement noise
ranked.summary: New preprints add noise models, confidence estimates and noise-corrected metrics to perturbation-response and spatial transcriptomics prediction.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that predictive omics models are being built and judged with explicit attention to measurement noise and reliability. For perturbation response, the Virtual Cell Challenge 2026 defines six metrics for zero-shot prediction of CRISPRi transcriptional responses. DeepCINET models viability assay noise in cancer cell line drug response ranking, and siGMA uses heteroscedastic uncertainty to handle noisy cross-dataset siRNA efficacy labels. GAIN predicts combinatorial single-cell responses as an additive baseline plus a learned interaction term. A parallel strand addresses imaging-based spatial transcriptomics. Dancer separates within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination, and SYNDRI, trained on simulated data, removes transcript spillover. For histology-to-expression prediction, REGAIN attaches per-prediction confidence, and a noise-corrected correlation metric (RSC) is proposed for benchmarking. BRIDGE (cross-tissue imputation on GTEx) and GASTON-VI (spatial gradients across samples) are adjacent. All are preprints, so reported gains remain unreviewed.

ranked.headline: Separating cell-type composition from within-cell state change in bulk and single-cell data
ranked.summary: New long-read methylation tools and large-scale transcriptomic decompositions aim to disentangle cell-type mixture effects from intrinsic state shifts.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is separating changes in cell-type composition from changes within cells. COMET assigns bulk long-read DNA reads to cell types using cell-type-specific methylation, separating composition shifts from within-cell changes in blood, brain and other tissues. LongReadClock applies the same logic to ageing, building cell-type-resolved epigenetic clocks from bulk blood long-read methylation data. At larger scale, a single-cell foundation model (UCE) spanning more than 59M cells across 614 states maps state bridges and composition remodeling. Robust multi-run ICA of 778 CHO RNA-seq samples yields 105 reproducible iModulons capturing lineage, stress and process-responsive states. Related work reports a small germ-layer imprint on transcriptomic ageing across 24 GTEx tissues, distinct multi-omic effects of individual CHIP driver genes, mucociliary programs in healthy endocervix and ectocervix, and a 12-gene neuroimmune signature in HPV-associated cervical cancer. What is new is the use of long-read methylation to resolve cell types directly from bulk samples. All findings remain preprint observations.

ranked.headline: Regulatory inference from multiomics is adjusting for confounders and calibrating noise
ranked.summary: New preprints adjust peak-gene and network inference for latent factors, perturbations and cross-modal discordance, and audit replicate-level noise floors.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is regulatory inference from multiomic and perturbational data, with explicit control of confounding and noise. CREMAP adjusts shared technical and biological latent variation before testing peak-gene links in single-cell multiome data. scOnion scores cell-level concordance between paired expression and chromatin accessibility rather than assuming the two modalities agree. Two works anchor inference in interventions. A TNBC framework combines CRISPRi Perturb-seq responses with TF-binding priors and nominates CTCF, MYC and AP-1 members as master regulators. ImmunoTwin maps CRISPR-screen regulators of T-cell and macrophage activation and reports a replicated coupling of T-cell exhaustion with macrophage M1 programs under checkpoint blockade. FiberTron predicts base-level chromatin, methylation and transcript patterns from Fiber-seq and nanopore RNA-seq of a single sample, which enables testing of variant effects. Two calibration studies set limits on interpretation. In drug-tolerant PC9 cells, replicate libraries define the noise floor for cell-state claims. Across 32,245 ATAC-seq experiments, text-metadata embeddings only weakly track accessibility similarity.

ranked.headline: Mapping regulatory RNAs, their binding partners and targets across bacteria to flies
ranked.summary: New preprints pair genome-wide maps, accessibility profiling and binding arrays to nominate RNA regulators and targets in bacteria, protists, yeast and Drosophila.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is systematic discovery of regulatory RNAs and their interaction partners. In bacteria, aureoRNA compiles phylogeny, transcriptome data and target predictions for Staphylococcus aureus sRNAs, revealing new targets such as those of RsaD. A separate study in E. coli profiles CsrA-dependent RNA accessibility to nominate new mRNA and sRNA targets, linking CsrA to polyphosphate levels and Hfq-containing HP-bodies. On the protein side, dsRBP-seq and protein domain arrays screen for direct dsRNA–domain interactions and identify STAU2 dsRBM3 binding to Sem1 dsRNA. Comparative genomics with CMfinder and R-scape adds seven candidate structured ncRNA motifs in protists, likely regulating genes including RuBisCO and phycocyanin. Two studies extend the theme in eukaryotes: multi-colour smFISH resolves distinct, RBP-dependent, cell-cycle-linked localization of the co-regulated yeast mRNAs SRL1 and SUN4, and small ORFs in Drosophila lncRNAs continue translating during heat shock, with some microproteins improving survival.

ranked.headline: New software lowers barriers to reproducible, private and species-resolved microbial genomic analysis
ranked.summary: Six preprints released 19–24 November extend microbiome, pathogen and metaproteomics analysis through interoperable, browser-based and reproducible tools.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is software that makes microbial sequence and proteomic analysis more accessible, interoperable and reproducible. VPHYL converts Emu and EPI2ME wf-16s nanopore 16S abundance tables into phyloseq and BIOM objects, while RADSuite pairs RADlib, a curated 16S rRNA gene copy database, with RADx to enable species-level identification. SNP2Cluster-Py clusters pathogen genomes by core SNP distance with epidemiological and temporal context, tested on Klebsiella and other data. Unipept's 2026 update brings multi-sample metaproteomics workflows into a web platform. Sparrowhawk uses WebAssembly for private in-browser microbial genomics, and a Fusion transpiler study tests whether SNHA network-inference code stays functionally identical across nine languages. The advances are at the tool level (workflow design, interoperability, privacy-preserving deployment, reproducibility) rather than new biological findings.

ranked.headline: Sex chromosome complement drives sex-biased gene expression across tissues and species
ranked.summary: New single-cell and isogenic hiPSC models separate sex chromosome effects from hormones and donor genotype, extending a cross-species prenatal dosage atlas.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is dissecting how sex chromosome complement shapes transcription independent of gonadal hormones. A cross-species single-cell atlas maps sex-biased expression and X-to-autosome dosage compensation across mouse and human prenatal development. In FCG rats, single-cell profiling with mouse comparison indicates that sex chromosome complement dominates gene regulation in the medial septum. An isogenic hiPSC-derived vascular smooth muscle platform contrasts monosomy-X and euploid lines and reports donor-specific transcriptomic effects. Sequencing of aged human nephron segments adds a somatic dimension, with chromosome 18 loss expanding in collecting duct clones. The dioxin-induced fetal uropathy study is largely unrelated to this thread, addressing renal developmental transcriptomics after chemical exposure.

ranked.headline: Network and landscape structure shape how movement and individual change scale to evolutionary outcomes
ranked.summary: Five new models link network topology, movement and social rewiring to host-parasite evolution, herbivore impacts and phenology under environmental change.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that network or spatial structure mediates how individual-level traits and behaviours scale to population, evolutionary and ecosystem outcomes. Simulations on 268 empirical social networks indicate that compensatory tie formation alters predicted consequences of individual loss. Host-parasite models show that degree heterogeneity in spatial networks shapes host resistance and spatial variation in parasite infectivity, and that parasite-impaired host mobility favours reduced virulence via relatedness and host density. A spatially explicit model links herbivore movement and landscape structure to resource depletion and population dynamics, and an individual-based model shows that social information use synchronises breeding but constrains tracking of rapid environmental change. What is new is the explicit coupling of movement, rewiring or information use to evolutionary and demographic responses. All items are simulation or theory based, so conclusions remain model-dependent.

ranked.headline: Genetic architecture, source identity and diversity loss shape adaptive persistence under change
ranked.summary: New stickleback, Boechera and wild-population genomic studies test which genetic features predict adaptation, persistence and erosion under environmental change.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is which genomic and population features determine whether populations adapt or persist under environmental change. Icelandic stickleback adapted to geothermal warming show distinct genetic architectures for within- and transgenerational plasticity. Replicated introductions across nine lakes indicate that source population identity predicts success better than environmental matching. In Boechera stricta, genome-environment analyses suggest hot, dry projected climates may exceed adaptive capacity. Declining yellow-bellied marmots show recent Ne and census collapse after 2010 with elevated inbreeding, while a bird study indicates that temporal genomic erosion estimates need demographic and technical validation because estimator and degradation biases can arise. New here is the emphasis on source effects, separable plasticity architectures, and methodological limits when inferring persistence from genomic data.

ranked.headline: Clock and transcriptional regulators time plant responses to heat, warming and drought
ranked.summary: New preprints tie CCA1/LHY heat responses, potato clock phase and autumn-warming networks to regulators of temperature and stress responses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how regulatory layers set the timing and magnitude of plant responses to temperature and related stress. In Arabidopsis, CCA1 and LHY mutants show time-of-day heat responses across transcriptome, proteome and metabolome, implicating sulfur, ROS and related processes. In cultivated potato, diel expression phase differs from wild Solanum species independently of clock period, with DOF and REVEILLE transcription factors linked to these shifts. In white spruce, autumn warming decouples photosynthesis and cold-acclimation gene networks from growth cessation, with MYB and AP2/ERF regulators involved. Wheat m6A and metabolomic profiling adds an epitranscriptomic layer to drought, and MEAM-OWL offers motif-expression analysis validated on pearl millet. The new emphasis is on timing and decoupling of regulatory programs rather than the earlier priming and organ-level stress-combination focus.

ranked.headline: Organelle quality control rewired by contact sites, lipid supply and induced degradation
ranked.summary: New work links copper sensing, ER-mitochondria contacts, lipid tethers and VCP-dependent ER degradation to how organelles are remodeled under stress.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a focus on how organelles are remodeled or cleared under stress, each through a distinct route. In mitochondria, copper binding to OXA1L disrupts mitoribosome assembly and releases MRPL20 to the nucleus, activating ATF5-driven UPRmt that restrains cuproptosis. In yeast, the ER-vacuole tether Mdm1 balances phospholipid and neutral lipid metabolism to support autophagosome completion. ATAD1 at mitochondria-ER contacts moves mislocalized Pex26 to the ER, and induced ubiquitination degrades ER membrane proteins via VCP-dependent extraction, bypassing canonical ERAD. In Arabidopsis, AtNBR1 transiently associates with lipid droplets during germination, linked to seed longevity. The new element is assignment of specific sensors, tethers and extraction factors to each context rather than a single shared mechanism. Previous claims on iron-deficiency pexophagy, Rab32 and RAB11-RAB30 are not supported by these items.

ranked.headline: Mechanical forces and matrix signaling shape vascular and lymphatic function in development and aging
ranked.summary: Five preprints link mechanical cues, ECM and signaling pathways to vascular and lymphatic phenotypes across development, aging and injury.
ranked.synthesis: The preprints converge loosely on how mechanical and matrix-related cues specify or maintain vessel and tissue function. In aging mouse collecting lymphatics, reduced SRF-driven contractility rather than smooth muscle cell loss underlies dilation and impaired drainage. Transmural compression impairs lymphatic endothelial barrier integrity and promotes inflammation via a Piezo1-CaMKII Ca2+ axis. In zebrafish choroid plexus, hemodynamic forces, klf2a/klf2b and Yap1/Wwtr1-dependent epithelial-endothelial Vegfab-Vegfr2 signaling establish fenestrated endothelial identity. Two developmental mouse studies concern matrix: neural crest Tmem2 loss causes cleft palate with HA accumulation, hypoxia and vascular defects, and stromal Ilk deletion disrupts fibronectin expression and renal tissue integrity within a defined time window. Together they emphasize mechanotransduction and ECM as determinants of vascular phenotype.

ranked.headline: Spatially restricted hormone and cell-polarity cues pattern root and floral organ growth
ranked.summary: Five preprints define domain-specific auxin perception, SBP-mediated repression and polarized expansin delivery as spatial determinants of plant organ form.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is spatial restriction of developmental signals in roots, with one floral counterpart. Domain-specific synthetic auxin perception in Arabidopsis roots indicates that outer elongating cells control root growth, and shifting the domain moves the proliferation zone. In Hibiscus trionum petals, auxin preserves bullseye proportions through distal cell behaviour but does not initiate the boundaries. In maize, SBP factors TSH4, UB2 and UB3 repress brace root initiation and primordia expansion via LG2 and gibberellin signalling. ROP activation recruits EXPA7 to root hair initiation sites by brefeldin-A-sensitive trafficking. Metaxylem number varies along wheat and grass root axes, linked to hydraulic modelling. Together these works separate initiation from proportion and expansion.

ranked.headline: Structured statistical models resolve donor, lineage, and spatial sources of single-cell variation
ranked.summary: Five preprints use structured latent and mixture models to separate heritable, environmental, and donor effects in single-cell and lineage-resolved data.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a focus on structured models that partition variation in single-cell data into interpretable sources. scPACE uses a hierarchical personalized variational autoencoder to represent cell and donor states in cohort transcriptomics and to impute missing cell types. SOUR separates heritable lineage effects from spatial microenvironment effects on tumor cell expression. ChronoClone groups clones into metaclones by time-resolved cell-state composition, revealing differences in clonal speed. ELLA-mix applies a count-conditioned finite mixture to identify cell subpopulations with distinct radial RNA localization in imaging-based spatial data. PRNODE jointly estimates mother and daughter yeast protein networks with a shared scaffold to quantify inheritance. The common emphasis is explicit modeling of inheritance, environment, and subcellular or temporal structure, rather than large pretrained embeddings alone.

ranked.headline: Sequence- and graph-based models predict protein, enzyme, glycan and ligand properties with bias and uncertainty control
ranked.summary: Five preprints show bias-aware and uncertainty-aware learning from sequence, structure and graphs across enzymes, glycans, docking and adverse-event prediction.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is predictive modelling of biomolecular function from sequence, structure or graph representations, with explicit handling of representation limits. CarmnaDD predicts nitrogenase activity from sequence alone with dual descriptors (R2 0.60, AUC 0.94) and maps informative windows onto NifH. SCOPE combines structure and evolutionary information in a residue-level graph model for catalytic residues, with mutagenesis validation. GlycanPUG applies heterogeneous graph pretraining on WURCS 2.0 to structurally ambiguous glycans. Two preprints address reliability: Inverse Node Frequency normalises metapath features to reduce hub bias in target-adverse event prediction, and a dependence-aware conformal framework with copula calibration provides 3D uncertainty intervals for docking. The new element is interpretability, debiasing and calibrated uncertainty added to predictors.

ranked.headline: Lysosomal programs in microglia and axons, plus a tau seeding modifier, shape neurodegeneration
ranked.summary: Five preprints link lysosomal state to microglial reprogramming and axonal quality control, with TRA2B lowering tau seeding thresholds and ankyrin-G tools for the AIS.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is lysosomal state as a determinant of neurodegenerative cell phenotypes. Two preprints tie lysosomal programs to disease-associated microglia (DAM): MiT/TFE-driven lysosomal biogenesis precedes and couples to DAM reprogramming across murine injury, amyloidosis and human AD, while GPNMB marks a reversible, TREM2-dependent lysosomal program that tracks neurodegeneration severity in FTD/AD models. In neurons, the axon initial segment is described as a lysosome quality-control checkpoint, with MCF2L anchoring lysosomes via gAnkG and retaining less acidic ones, and a separate preprint engineers a high-affinity ankyrin-G binder for targeting the AIS. A further preprint identifies TRA2B as a latent endogenous modifier that lowers the tau seeding threshold. New here is the focus on lysosomal programs as measurable, compartment-specific readouts that scale with pathology.

ranked.headline: Perinatal and environmental perturbations reshape specific neural cell populations in mice
ranked.summary: Four mouse studies link neonatal, maternal, genetic, or environmental perturbations to cell-type-specific changes in cortex, hippocampus, and prefrontal circuits.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is cell-type-resolved readout of mouse brain after a defined perturbation. Neonatal SARS-CoV-2 spike protein exposure was associated with region-specific changes in SOX2 cells and TBR1 neurons at P10, without broad cerebrovascular or BBB alterations. Constitutive 5-HT2A deletion in BALB/c mice was linked to anxiety-like behavior, reduced hippocampal parvalbumin, and lower energy-metabolism protein levels. An enriched environment raised prefrontal perineuronal nets through NRG1/ErbB4 signaling and aggrecan, with improved cognition in adult mice. In the one published study, maternal TPOAb exposure caused placental inflammation, fetal BBB disruption, hippocampal microglial activation, and altered BDNF/synaptic signaling. The new element is the focus on specific cell populations, including progenitors, interneurons, and microglia, though most evidence is preprint-stage and associative.

ranked.headline: Core metabolic enzymes and cofactor pathways couple to ROS, immunity and development in plants and algae
ranked.summary: New work links Calvin cycle, malic enzyme, isochorismate synthase and FAD synthase perturbations to redox stress, immunity and organ development.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a focus on how perturbing single metabolic enzymes or cofactor pathways reshapes stress physiology and development. In Chlamydomonas, loss or inhibition of PRK in the Calvin cycle triggers light-dependent ROS and autophagy, with ATG8 loss aggravating photosynthetic stress. In Arabidopsis, NAD-malic enzyme subunits ME1 and ME2 show asymmetric interdependence, alter the proteome and metabolism, and affect early fungal penetration. In tomato, knockout of the sole isochorismate synthase lowers pathogen-induced salicylic acid and Pto resistance and impairs phylloquinone-dependent chloroplast function. Arabidopsis cytosolic FAD synthase influences flavin homeostasis, FAD-to-FMN ratios, leaf pigmentation and floral organ development through phytohormone changes. The common thread is metabolic enzymes acting as nodes linking redox, immunity and development.

ranked.headline: Metagenomics and RNA sequencing uncover novel viral lineages in kelp and deep seawater
ranked.summary: New sequencing surveys expand known viral diversity in kelp, mesopelagic seawater and CRESS DNA viruses, including algal and fungal endogenous elements.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is sequence-based discovery of viral diversity in algal and marine systems. An RNA virome of New Zealand bull kelp reveals novel viral lineages, with higher diversity at a city-proximal site and in unhealthy kelp. Long-read metagenomics of mesopelagic Andaman Sea seawater yields 1,604 high-confidence viral contigs, mostly bacteriophages, with genomic novelty. A phylogenetic survey of CRESS DNA viruses combines environmental metagenomes, reference genomes and fungal and algal endogenous viral elements, revealing unclassified lineages. What is new is the combination of long-read and host-associated or genome-embedded sources to resolve previously unexplored viral clades. A dengue genomic epidemiology study from Ivory Coast is a distinct, host-specific outlier within the group and does not share this thread.

ranked.headline: Kinase-driven remodeling of ER-plasma membrane contacts and cortex coordinates cell division
ranked.summary: Fresh reports link mitotic phosphorylation to ER-PM contact loss and cortical remodeling, alongside kinase-phosphatase and cytoskeletal control of division and secretion.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is phosphorylation-controlled reorganization of cellular architecture during division. In one preprint, mitosis-specific phosphorylation of the ER-plasma membrane tether E-Syt2 drives loss of ERPM contact sites, and retaining them delays cell progression. In fission yeast, Pdk1 phosphorylates the eisosome component Pil1 to disassemble eisosomes and remodel plasma membrane and cortical ER at the division site for Mid1 recruitment. A structural preprint on the CPC-PP2A(B56) hub, mediated by Borealin motifs, extends the kinase-phosphatase theme to chromosome segregation fidelity. The MTCL1/2 study is less directly mitotic, but shows katanin and CAPZ recruitment coordinating Golgi-region microtubules and actin to support secretory vesicle docking. New here is the mechanistic resolution of phosphoregulatory nodes at membrane contacts, cortex, and segregation machinery.

ranked.headline: Light cues and dormancy shape behavior in Hydra and Drosophila
ranked.summary: Newly posted preprints and a published study report divergent light-driven and sleep-related behaviors among closely related strains and species.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is behavioral divergence among genetically similar lines or species, with light input and sleep-related states as recurring variables. In Hydra vulgaris, two closely related F1 strains from the AEP line differ in phototaxis under starvation: AEP Irvine wanders, whereas AEP Kiel shows positive phototaxis. In Drosophila, cold-induced dormancy promotes large huddles away from food, and NPF signaling regulates both feeding and huddling, with the two separable from appetite-driven effects. Artificially selected early and late eclosion chronotype lines show correlated divergence in sleep architecture, sleep fragmentation and recovery. A published study reports species-specific photopreference of Drosophila species for rhythmic flickering light beyond the perceptual flicker frequency. The new element is the dissociation of behavioral outputs, including aggregation site choice from feeding and sleep architecture linked to chronotype.

ranked.headline: Aquatic stressors alter behaviour and physiology in invertebrates and fish
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and published studies report context-dependent stress responses, including noise-driven behaviour changes in Oikopleura dioica across life stages.
ranked.synthesis: The current items share a focus on how stressors modify organismal performance in aquatic taxa, with responses depending on context rather than being fixed. In the Oikopleura dioica preprint, anthropogenic noise alters behaviour in a life stage- and signal-specific way, with larvae appearing most sensitive. A meta-analysis of freshwater invertebrates and fish reports that sublethal chemical exposure lowers heat tolerance and increases its variability. In Dermasterias imbricata, food availability modifies physiological and behavioural responses to prolonged thermal stress, and in cyprinid fish hypoxia tolerance differs between lentic and lotic species. The new element is the explicit treatment of contextual modifiers, such as life stage, nutritional state and habitat, as determinants of stress responses. Only the Dermasterias and cyprinid studies are published; the Oikopleura and meta-analysis findings are preprints and remain provisional. Sound-specific evidence is limited to the Oikopleura preprint.

ranked.headline: Distributed brain organization varies with cognitive state and task demands
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply 7T fMRI, information decomposition and network dynamics to test state-dependent brain organization across cognitive tasks.
ranked.synthesis: Across these preprints the dominant thread is that distributed brain networks are described through state-dependent, low-dimensional dynamics. A 7T fMRI and encoding-model study reports load-tuned topographic maps across a fronto-parieto-occipital network during visual working memory. An fMRI oddball study finds that auditory and visual target detection share low-dimensional brain-state dimensions, with modality-dependent later trajectories. Information decomposition of fMRI recorded during feature films maps distributed storage, transfer and transformation in the naturalistic human brain. Pulse-DOT PReFx estimates of regional arterial elasticity in cortical networks relate to cognitive control costs in a task-switching paradigm. A signed dynamic connectivity framework links subcortical routing modes to whole-brain network flexibility and behavioral traits. The new element is the joint use of state-dependent measures and low-dimensional network descriptions across perceptual, memory, control and naturalistic paradigms.

ranked.headline: Nanopore and amplification methods extend molecular identification to archival samples
ranked.summary: Long-read and low-input methods now recover species identities and genomes from century-old and single-larva material.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is molecular inference of species identity, diversity and genomic features from limited or archival material. Nanopore sequencing underpins a barcoding survey of 3,657 European Ulva samples from 30 countries, identifying 46 species and flagging non-indigenous taxa, and a mini-barcoding workflow that recovered COI sequences from 284 of 288 century-old spider museum specimens, adding 53 new BINs to BOLD. Multiple displacement amplification enables WGS and GBS genotyping of single zebra mussel veliger larvae from about 1 ng DNA. Off-target sequencing of 312 spruce bark beetles reveals frequent nematode associates across Europe, and a Nanopore-based annotated reference genome is reported for the Critically Endangered Bermuda skink. What is new is the application of these approaches to low-input and century-old material.

ranked.headline: Pangenome and haplotype-resolved references reshape plant genotype-trait interpretation
ranked.summary: Five preprints show that reference choice and haplotype-resolved genomes alter the genetic interpretation of plant traits and RNA-seq measurements.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is that genotype-linked interpretation depends on the reference framework. A parent-of-origin-resolved Granny Smith apple genome shows that matched references expose sun-exposure and cold-storage responses that other references miss. In Capsicum, a 48-genome super-pangenome resolves structural variation and NLR resistance gene diversity, while a pangenome-guided k-mer GWAS links pungency and aroma terpene traits to Pun1 haplotypes and TPS genes. Mapping strategy is a related variable: a comparison of genome-guided and transcriptome-guided RNA-seq quantification across six plant species reports quantification bias for tandemly duplicated genes. The Tipularia discolor study, based on a fragmented assembly, mines candidate genes for sucrose, terpenoid and phenylpropanoid metabolism. What is new is the use of haplotype-resolved and pangenome frameworks to resolve allele-specific and reference-dependent variation.

ranked.headline: Somatic mutational processes are being resolved from chromosomes to indels across human tissues
ranked.summary: Cell-free DNA now reports tissue somatic mutations non-invasively as InDel and chromosome-level analyses refine mutational process attribution.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread across these preprints is the resolution at which somatic change is measured in tissues, from chromosome number and structure to indel classes. In acral melanoma, single-cell chromosome counts range from 25 to over 200, with continuous numerical and cryptic structural fluctuation linked to MMBIR repair. Two cell-free DNA studies extend detection of clonal mosaicism and liver-derived somatic mutations to chronic liver disease and ulcerative colitis, reporting etiology-linked patterns without tissue sampling. A genome-wide InDel taxonomy of 887 multiple myeloma genomes adds a distinct class of mutational processes, including a TXNDC5 hotspot and an association with treatment outcome. A benchmarking study of sample mispairing detection tools addresses sample-identity verification in multimodal cancer datasets, a methodological concern distinct from mutational processes themselves.

ranked.headline: Multi-omic layers define glycan and transcriptional states in tumors
ranked.summary: Integrating proteomics, glycoproteomics and transcriptomics across cohorts now exposes molecular links to ovarian and pancreatic cancer.
ranked.synthesis: The five preprints share an emphasis on integrating multiple molecular layers to define tumor regulatory states. Matched serum proteomics and intact N-glycoproteomics of 100 participants, analysed with a new differential-trend-subtype (DTS) framework, link glycan remodelling to ovarian cancer. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, PDAC BioPortal unifies bulk, single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomic cohorts, while spatial transcriptomics of CA19-9-positive regions yields four transcriptional programs associated with survival and cell-line drug sensitivity. PTMlink scores glycosylation–phosphorylation co-variation across 1,211 tumor proteomes, and PathwayTheme reverses the usual PCA workflow by decomposing per-sample pathway scores to test pathway-level axes of variation. The common thread is methodological and resource-oriented: cross-layer co-variation and pathway-level axes are made testable rather than inferred from single modalities.

ranked.headline: Testing interpretability and causal structure in biological deep learning models
ranked.summary: Deep learning models for transcriptomics, proteins and pathology are now being tested against curated annotations and perturbation data.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is a move from reporting predictive accuracy toward asking what learned representations actually encode. In transcriptomic and protein settings, interpretability claims are checked against external reference points: sparse autoencoder features on transcriptomic foundation models largely act as gene detectors on spatial panels, and conclusions from interpretability methods in protein language models (ESMC) depend on residue-level curated annotations. Other items build structure into the model instead of inspecting it after training. CIRCE applies a Boltzmann distribution over Hamming distance in combinatorial perturbation space to infer both input identity and graded signaling strength. CMC-VAE links genes and proteins causally across CITE-seq data and reports improved perturbation predictions after interventions. SimpleP2G addresses a different question, comparing image encoders and decoder designs for predicting gene expression from pathology images, with Virchow2 features and a simple frozen-embedding decoder highlighted.

ranked.headline: Predicted templates and consensus ranking refine antibody-antigen structure models
ranked.summary: Four new preprints target sampling, model selection, and epitope guidance to improve antibody-antigen structure prediction.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is improving antibody-antigen complex structure prediction by working around the limits of single predictors. AbPoolRank ranks mixed structure pools with a predictor-agnostic consensus, reaching 58.0% Success@1. A separate preprint adds PIPER rigid-body docking templates to AlphaFold 3 and Boltz-2, raising success from 56.2% to 63.4% in a leakage-free evaluation. APEs uses an agentic system that retrieves public evidence to predict ranked residue-level epitopes, guiding complex sampling and model selection. What is new is the shift from tuning a single model toward external inputs and selection layers: docking-derived templates, epitope predictions, and consensus ranking. The SPACE-TCR preprint is heterogeneous to this thread; it groups paired αβ TCR structures by CDR loop geometry to recover antigen-specific convergent receptor families beyond sequence similarity.

ranked.headline: CTCF function depends on genomic context; transcription forms insulation boundaries
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test CTCF target recognition in yeast and transcription-driven boundary formation, extending insulation models beyond cohesin.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how CTCF-associated architecture and chromatin boundaries are established. A naive-genome study expressing human CTCF in budding yeast reports that it localizes to chromatin but binds specific sites weakly and does not robustly drive transcription, suggesting target recognition depends on evolutionary context. A second preprint shows that transcription activation at the Fbn2 locus forms cohesin-independent decompaction and insulation, while transcriptional bursts disrupt CTCF looping, analyzed by Micro-C. AMBER maps accessible-chromatin associations into multi-scale regulatory hubs in mouse brain, and a yeast study addresses how intrinsically disordered regions modulate DNA binding by Msn2, Msn4 and Com2. These items are heterogeneous; the new element is that insulation can arise from transcription independently of cohesin-driven barrier formation.

ranked.headline: PP2A-B55α Terminates Mitophagy by Selectively Dephosphorylating Parkin via a Non-Canonical Interface
ranked.summary: PP2A-B55 holoenzyme terminates PINK1-Parkin mitophagy by dephosphorylating pParkin via a non-canonical B55 interface binding the folded Parkin Ubl domain; a…

ranked.headline: Regulatory elements and progenitor genes shape human cortical development
ranked.summary: Single-cell and cross-species multiomic atlases now resolve human-enriched cortical progenitor and enhancer programs at mid-gestation.
ranked.synthesis: The four preprints converge on the developing human cortex, where regulatory and progenitor programs are being resolved at single-cell and cross-species resolution. Human-specific transposable elements are reported in cortical organoids to regulate the timing of the radial glia-to-neuron transition, with locus-resolved single-cell long-read profiling paired with CRISPRi-based manipulation. Cross-species multiomics of human, macaque and mouse fetal cortex identifies RHOJ as an outer radial glia-enriched regulator of human-enriched progenitor states. A single-nucleus chromatin accessibility atlas of 1.17 million candidate enhancers across 104,000 mid-gestation cortical nuclei provides a lineage-restricted regulatory reference. VEGABrain complements these resources as an open web tool that projects bulk RNA-seq and ssGSEA gene-set enrichment onto human brain atlas surfaces across developmental stages. The shared thread is the mapping of human-specific regulatory and progenitor states, while VEGABrain is a visualization resource rather than an experimental result.

ranked.headline: Linking Molecular Changes in the Hypothalamus to Alzheimer's Disease Phenotypes
ranked.summary: Single-nucleus RNA-seq of 1.1 million hypothalamic nuclei in AD-BXD mice reveals sex-biased, cell-type-specific amyloid responses linked to early non-cognitive…

ranked.headline: Signaling history and regulators calibrate macrophage and microglia immune responses
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show prior exposure and viral proteins reshape innate immune outputs across human, avian, and microglial systems.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread across these preprints is that prior state and cell identity, not acute stimulation alone, calibrate the magnitude and composition of innate immune output. In primary human macrophages, earlier cytokine exposure constrains subsequent transcriptional responses, with IFNβ dominating. Syngeneic iPSC-derived microglia-like and CAM-like macrophages display distinct TLR-driven NF-κB responses, differing HIV permissiveness, and varied cART responses. In microglia-like cells, Zika virus NS2B suppresses the PA28 immunoproteasome during the innate antiviral response. A modeling study links cytokine feedback to strain-specific immune responses to avian coronavirus. What is new is the explicit dependence of these responses on signaling history and on macrophage lineage, with viral proteins and feedback loops acting as modifiers of that calibration.

ranked.headline: Sequencing reveals mutation rates and genome composition across vertebrates and plants
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply long-read sequencing and barcoded tracing to genome assembly accuracy, mutation rates, and neuronal projections.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of high-accuracy sequencing and barcoding to quantify genomic and cellular variation across taxa. Cortical neuron point mutation rates estimated with PacBio HiFi sequencing reach about 25.9 mutations per diploid genome per year, similar in mice and humans. A separate preprint models equilibrium trinucleotide genome composition from context-dependent mutation spectra in 25 plant and 10 mammalian species, incorporating GC-biased gene conversion. A sequencing-based barcoded connectomics method maps single-neuron projections rapidly across seven vertebrate species, from frogs to primates. Meanwhile, a critique argues that the 'near T2T' Canton-S Drosophila assembly is inconsistent with three other independent Canton-S assemblies, raising questions about reference accuracy. The new elements are the cross-species scale of mutation and composition modelling and the barcoded projection mapping, which together extend sequencing from reference assembly to neuronal and mutational inference.

ranked.headline: Thylakoid pH and proton fluxes shape photosynthetic regulation in plants
ranked.summary: Four late-November 2026 preprints dissect proton and pH dynamics controlling photosynthetic light regulation in Arabidopsis and Chlamydomonas.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the control of proton and ion fluxes across the thylakoid membrane and their coupling to photosynthetic regulation. A mutagenesis study in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii identifies conserved subunit-IV residue PetD:D35 as essential for proton resupply and Q-cycle efficiency at the cytochrome b6f stromal Qn site. In Arabidopsis, PsbS mutants with altered lumenal protonation sites show a small, zeaxanthin- and acidification-linked energy-dependent quenching, pointing to complexity in PsbS protonation. NHD1, a thylakoid Na+/H+ antiporter, supports acclimation to fluctuating light and shows partial redundancy with KEA3 and VCCN1. A comparison of four genetically encoded pH biosensors identifies pHluorin2 for imaging light-driven stromal and lumen pH dynamics in living Arabidopsis and Chlamydomonas. What is new is the in vivo readout of these proton-handling processes alongside molecular dissection of their components.

ranked.headline: Genome-scale data untangle discordant phylogenies in rapid radiations and deep splits
ranked.summary: Four new preprints apply gene-dense, duplication-aware and whole-genome methods to resolve conflicting relationships across eukaryotes and deer.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the use of genome-scale data to resolve phylogenetic conflict, with each preprint addressing a different source of discordance. In Aizoaceae, phylotranscriptomic data resolve major relationships, but short internodes limit resolution within the rapid radiation. Reconciliation of 219 pre-LECA ancient gene duplication families is used to test candidate root positions of the eukaryote tree. The H2O workflow targets detection of large-scale gene family expansions, combining Ks distributions, tree-based duplication calls and paralogy-aware filtering. In Old World deer, whole-genome data attribute Miocene divergences mainly to incomplete lineage sorting, whereas Pliocene-Pleistocene splits show a gene flow contribution. What is new is the attention to data density, duplication history and the separation of sorting from introgression as distinct sources of discordance.

ranked.headline: Thalamic firing and prefrontal-amygdala circuits shape sleep and fear learning
ranked.summary: Recent preprints link neuronal firing, developmental wiring and circuit engagement to sleep, fear extinction and motor output.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how defined neuronal populations and their connections establish circuit function. In the thalamus, conditional knockout of Shox2 in VPM neurons reduces tonic and burst firing of thalamocortical neurons, impairing whisker-based behavior and sleep spindles in mice. In fear learning, juvenile mice do not engage mPFC-amygdala circuitry during extinction, and optogenetic potentiation of this pathway accelerates adult-type extinction. A developmental timeline of lateral olfactory tract innervation of piriform cortex is mapped from embryonic to postnatal stages using calretinin and tdTomato labeling. Corticofugal output neurons arising from direct versus indirect neurogenesis differ transcriptomically and are compared functionally in motor cortex during a reach-grasp-drink task. The most mechanistically specific evidence comes from the thalamic and prefrontal items, where manipulation of firing or pathway activity is tied to behavior; the olfactory and corticofugal items are primarily descriptive or lineage-based.

ranked.headline: Dopamine signaling and alpha-synuclein reshape striatal and midbrain neuron function
ranked.summary: Four November 2026 preprints link dopamine tone, D1 signaling loss and alpha-synuclein overexpression to altered dopaminergic and striatal neuron function.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how dopamine signaling and dopaminergic neurons, including those in Parkinson's-relevant models, shape cell-type-specific striatal and midbrain function and behavior. Tonic dopamine is shown to regulate PKA activity differently in D1 and D2 neurons and to modulate reward-motivated behavior. In a 6-OHDA mouse model, prolonged loss of D1 receptor signaling is reported to make direct-pathway striatal projection neurons hyperresponsive to dopamine. Overexpression of human alpha-synuclein in midbrain dopamine neurons produces progressive action-outcome learning deficits and impaired reversal learning. A human Anxa1-associated dopaminergic population, transferred from mouse, is most depleted in Parkinson's brains and likely innervates caudal putamen. Together these preprints add cell-type resolution to dopamine-dependent plasticity and link a specific neuronal population to disease vulnerability.

ranked.headline: Host identity and eukaryotic bycatch shape marine and global microbiome datasets
ranked.summary: Host identity structures marine holobiont communities, while metaEukaryome shows eukaryotic reads hidden in global metagenomes.
ranked.synthesis: Current items link microbial community structure to host identity and to eukaryotes recovered as bycatch in bacterial-focused sequencing. A 16S amplicon survey of the Antarctic stalked jellyfish Haliclystus antarcticus compares bacterial communities across gut, peduncle and tentacles, and reports antimicrobial activity from a gut-associated Oceanisphaera ostreae isolate. A three-year 16S survey of four South Florida octocoral species finds that host identity drives stable microbiomes dominated by host-specific Endozoicomonas. Across these marker-gene studies, host identity is the organizing variable. In contrast, metaEukaryome uses mitochondrial and plastid sequences to detect eukaryotes in 75,727 global metagenomes, revealing cross-domain co-occurrence. The new element is that eukaryotic sequences present in bacterial metagenome datasets can be systematically recovered and analysed.
